title: Caffeine-driven infra log
content:
Start-of-shift brain dump (coffee level: high).

— Top priorities for the first 45m:
  1) Quick health sweep: control plane, racks 4/5/6, edge region eu-west-2 (possible flaps last night).
     - Check: node-exporter for racks 4/5/6, diff in GPU temp vs baseline.
     - Quick commands: 
       * kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep 'gpu|edge'
       * kubectl top nodes | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 12
       * gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=redwood-gpu" --zones=all
  2) Capacity comfort: confirm headroom for morning batch jobs (08:00-10:00 PT).
     - Target: maintain >= 20% free GPU capacity for burst + rollout canaries.
     - Current rough numbers from last night: pool-1 active 78/96, pool-2 active 34/40.
     - If pool-1 > 85% for >10m -> start auto-burst (policy: burst-up to +8 gpus) or trigger handoff.
  3) Prewarm models used by hosted-api spike: opt-13b-int8, redwood-chat-7b.
     - Action: send 20 short prewarm requests across regions (eu/na/apac) to populate KV cache; check latency delta.
     - Script: scripts/prewarm/prewarm-loop.sh --model opt-13b-int8 --count 20 --regions na eu apac

— Things to fix/observe (notes to self):
  - Network: intermittent 5xx from router-nat-3 between 02:20-02:45 UTC. Likely route-reflection glitch; check BGP logs and ask netops for any maintenance windows.
  - Autoscaler logs for pool-2 show repeated scaling down that might be evicting long-running caches; open a short ticket if pattern persists (INFRA-4621 referenced).
  - Rolling upgrade checklist item: verify kernel-5.10 compat for new quant kernels. If not, schedule small canary on rack-6.

— Quick todo (checkbox style):
  [ ] run prewarm script for opt-13b-int8 (regions: na, eu)
  [ ] verify pool-1 utilization and consider increasing burst-limit to +10 GPUs (temp)
  [ ] post a short note in #infra-pager about nat-3 flaps and tagging netops
  [ ] escalate to SRE if node temps > 85C for >5m after throttling
  [ ] snapshot kube-scheduler metrics and upload to drive (link back here)

— Short commands/snippets I keep forgetting:
  - Check pod eviction timeline: kubectl get events --field-selector type=Warning --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | grep Evicted -n
  - Inspect GPU driver errors: sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service --since "2 hours ago" | tail -n 200
  - Rapid reclaim idle: scripts/pool/reclaim-idle.sh --pool pool-1 --threshold 30m

— Thoughts / ad-hoc metrics I want to track today:
  * 95p inference latency delta prewarm vs cold-start for opt-13b-int8 (goal: < 120ms extra per request)
  * per-token cost sensitivity when switching from int8->int4 quant for small-chat workloads (prod-3 route)
  * number of distinct model cache entries per node (to tune KV cache TTL)

— Questions / follow-ups:
  - Maya: did we push the autoscaler fix for the downscale thrash? If not, I should revert the policy.
  - Jian: want to pair on kernel compatibility canary at 11:30 — two-node pool test.
  - Ops: confirm if netops did any route maintenance overnight. If they did, tag in incident doc.

— End-of-shift handoff notes I will leave for next person:
  * If pool-1 stays >85% for 15m, leave the auto-burst enabled and notify on-call SRE.
  * If NAT flaps continue, escalate to netops and attach packet captures from nat-3.
  * Move any outstanding TODOs into the INFRA triage board (label: morning-shift).

Rough time log: 
  06:02 - start (boot cup 1)
  06:12 - checked node temps, one GPU at 87C -> throttled, notified Noah
  06:28 - kicked prewarm for opt-13b-int8 (na, eu)
  06:44 - saw a dip in 95p latency for redwood-chat-7b after 8 prewarm requests

Random brain-snippet: if we expose a "prewarm-as-a-service" small API, teams could request short-lived warmups before launches — but need cost guardrails.

Unresolved: whether to increase pool-1 burst limit (safety vs cost). I lean to +8 for the morning window only.

— Quick links I used:
  - capacity dashboard: https://dash.redwood.com/capacity/pool-views
  - incident NAT-3 logs: https://logs.redwood.com/query?range=2h&source=nat-3
  - autoscaler PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1283

End.
